pr_title: argspec - fix validating type for required options that are None
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
Fixes #79656

Fix skipping validating the type for all options that are None, even when None is not the default (e.g. when the option is required).

pr_comments: This PR only seems to cover `required`, but not `required_together`, `required_if`, etc., reported in #69190, which have the same problem. (See also my PR #72248 from 2020.)

@felixfontein They're related issues, but I don't think this really replaces anything in #72248. This enforces (non-str) type-validation for required options (it was always skipped for None), but it does not directly disallow None for required options or attempt to fix the more general issue in https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/69190.

Also this just needs a review, but probably won't happen until next week at the soonest, I am wrapping up feature-work.
@s-hertel looks like I didn't look at this closely enough. Sorry for the noise :)

issue_context.title: Argument spec validation for required dict var does not fail if dict var is set to None
issue_context.body:
### Summary

If the argument spec defines a dict variable as required:

- if the variable has no default in defaults/main.yml and is not provided in the playbook, argument spec validation will fail. That's OK.
- if the variable is defined as a string e.g. `''` or `'test-string'`, validation will fail. That's OK.
- if the variable is defines as None or `~`, validation will pass. That's NOT OK.

review_comments: 2 other things to consider `choices` and type `raw`

I have a test for raw validating that None is a valid value for a required raw option.

`choices` are checked after type coercion, and we don't validate `choices` match the `type`, so I think this improves internally consistency. This spec `dict(required=True, choices=[None, 'other_choice'])` would previously allow None. But it's ambiguous because the type is 'str', so imo it should be either
`dict(required=True, type='raw', choices=[None, 'other_choice'])`
or
`dict(required=True, choices=['None', 'other_choice'])`

Previous to the change in lib/ansible/module_utils/common/parameters.py, `None` string options were never converted to `'None'` because the type enforcement was skipped for all None values. However with my change, the type is now validated for required options and options that have a non-None default.

Returning 'None' would be a breaking change for `apt_repository`, which relies on None as a valid value for the **required** str option [`repo`](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/apt_repository_module.html#parameter-repo).

I waffled between two ways to fix this. Either do this, and update the `apt_repository` tests since `None` will now fail type conversion (what I did), or return None as-is just above (requires no update to the tests, but I wasn't sure if it makes sense for `check_type_str` to return a Nonetype).

```python
    if isinstance(value, string_types) or value is None:
        return value
```
